title: A finite type module with proper support is universally pure, and a proper morphism gives universal purity

standard_prerequisites.name: Factorisation of a module through its scheme theoretic support
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, Section morphisms-section-support, invoked at proof line 5034; Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-supported-on-closed, invoked at proof line 5036
standard_prerequisites.use: Writes the module as the pushforward of a finite type module on its scheme theoretic support, so that part (1) reduces to part (2).

standard_prerequisites.name: A proper morphism is universally closed
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, elementary property of proper morphisms used at proof lines 5041-5042
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that an impurity cannot exist, since the closure of the point would have to meet the special fibre, contradicting the definition of an impurity.

core_obligations: Reduce part (1) to part (2): write the module as the pushforward of a module on its scheme theoretic support, which is proper over the base by assumption, and apply the statement on modules supported on a closed subscheme (proof lines 5028-5036).

Rule out impurities in the proper case: given an impurity, universal closedness of the proper morphism makes the base change closed, so the image of the closure meets the special fibre, contradicting the defining property of an impurity (proof lines 5038-5043).
Read off the remaining parts: part (3) is the special case of part (2) for the structure sheaf (proof line 5024).
proof_roadmap: Part (3) as a special case (proof line 5024).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that a finite type module whose support is proper over the base is universally pure, and in particular that a proper morphism makes a finite type module, and the scheme itself, universally pure (statement lines 5015-5026, tag 05L3-adjacent). The proof reduces the first part to the case of a proper morphism by factoring the module through its support and then rules out impurities by universal closedness of a proper morphism. The contradiction argument is the substance, so the claim is H2.
